# Restart state: Gaussian cone separation after auditing the bound-entangled family

Date: 2026-10-08. Status: **internal proof package, not external validation or priority clearance**. No parallel subagents. No proof assistant. No claim of a historic-scale breakthrough.

## Strongest exact conclusions

1. For every integer r>=1 and d>=2^23 r^3, there exists a unital trace-preserving positive map P:M_d(C)->M_d(C), invariant under input and output transpose, such that P and P* are r-entanglement breaking but P is indecomposable. In fact its diamond distance from the decomposable cone is at least 6/55. P is not CP and is not a physical channel.
2. For every d>=2^23 k, there is a real full-rank PPT state rho, invariant under partial transpose with marginals I/d, at half-trace distance at least 7/3200 from the trace-one base of S_k+Gamma(S_k). The necessary decomposable-Schmidt level for all d-dimensional PPT maps therefore has order Theta(d). The exact level at each finite d, including d=4, remains unresolved here.
3. The physical unital TP PPT channels with Choi d*rho can be chosen to have entanglement-breaking index exactly two. This separates high decomposable-Schmidt complexity from iteration length; it does not refute PPT-cubed.

The first result negatively answers Devendra–Mallick–Sumesh Open Problem 1 under Definition 3.1 in arXiv:2105.14991v2. The second gives the asymptotic order in Park Question 5.11, arXiv:2608.13551v2. Both are mathematical conclusions of the written derivation; independent specialist checking is still required. A targeted search did not locate the statements but did locate closely related Gaussian and PT-invariant high-Schmidt methods, so priority is not established.

## Exact construction

Take V_d=traceless real symmetric matrices, HS-orthonormal basis S_a, h=d(d+1)/2-1, and iid real standard Gaussian g_ab. Set

    G=(1/d) sum_ab g_ab S_a tensor S_b,
    rho=(I+G/6)/d^2,
    W=I-32G,
    J(P)=W/d,
    J(Lambda)=d*rho.

G is invariant under both local partial transposes and has zero partial traces. The main finite-dimensional events are

    ||G||_op<5,
    Tr G^2>9d^2/40,
    q_k(G)<1/64                       [linear hierarchy]
    q_r(G)<1/(64r)                    [genuine r-EB],

where q_k is the supremum of the complex bilinear form over unit vectors of Schmidt rank <=k. An explicit rank-net argument gives

    Pr(q_k>eta)<=4

# Reassessment, route selection, and exact failed-transfer certificates

Research date: 8 October 2026. No parallel agents, external reviewers, proof assistants, or physical experiments were used. Prior files were read with the Files connector; repository state was read through GitHub at the immutable revisions below. This is an audit and new mathematical derivation, not a status upgrade by ingestion.

## 1. What survives from the old construction

The supplied candidate defines, for N=2n,

    R_N = Z_N^(-1) sum_(j=0)^n P_(N,j)/(2j+1)!!,

where the projectors contain all multiplicity spaces. The core algebra checks out in the reconstructed interfaces: common-rotation and permutation averaging gives singlet-pair/coherent-product decompositions; singleton partial transpose reduces to h_j <= (2j+3) h_(j+1); saturation gives the double-factorial coefficients. Twirling arbitrary singleton-PPT competitors preserves their total-spin law, so monotone reweighting gives the stated stochastic spin optimum. Dense states for N=2,4,6,8 and an independent symbolic N=4 reconstruction agree with these facts.

The arbitrary-identical-channel argument retains a specific external premise: quantum Sinkhorn normalization for a strictly positive qubit map by invertible input and output filters. The exact common-filter determinant identity on a singlet lets the input filter be replaced by a scalar inside each pair. The factorial sector weights control every fixed exponential reweighting of the unpaired spins. Boundary channels are handled by first adding a fixed sufficiently small amount of local depolarization, not by assuming invertible normalization there. The channel must be identical at all sites. Arbitrary site-dependent noise does not meet the determinant identity.

The imported normal-form statement and hypotheses were checked in Filippov 2021 Section II, which attributes the theorem to earlier operator-scaling work. It was not independently reproved. The separate unital two-qubit entanglement-annihilation criterion remains the published Filippov–Rybár–Ziman theorem, not a new result of the old construction.
